message.content:
**Operating efficiency and profitability, FY2022–FY2024 (Norfolk Southern Corp., CIK 702165)**

Using the latest annual report (10-K for FY2024, accession 0000702165-25-000008, filed 2025-02-10), which contains all three years on a consistent basis:

| Metric | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Railway operating revenues | $12,745M | $12,156M | $12,123M |
| Railway operating expenses | $7,936M | $9,305M | $8,052M |
| Income from railway operations | $4,809M | $2,851M | $4,071M |
| Net income | $3,270M | $1,827M | $2,622M |
| Operating ratio (op. exp./op. rev.) | 62.3% | 76.5% | 66.4% |
| Operating margin (op. income/op. rev.) | 37.7% | 23.5% | 33.6% |
| Net margin | 25.7% | 15.0% | 21.6% |

**What changed**
- **2023: sharp deterioration.** Revenue fell ~4.6% while operating expenses jumped ~17%, pushing the operating ratio up 14.2 points (62.3% → 76.5%) and cutting operating income 41% and net income 44%. The FY2024 10-K attributes this to costs of responding to the Eastern Ohio derailment (about $1.1B of expense, per the non-GAAP reconciliation), lower revenues (lower fuel surcharge and intermodal storage revenue), and higher non-incident operating expenses.
- **2024: partial recovery.** Revenue was roughly flat (−0.3%), but operating expenses fell 13% (including $433M of gains on railway-line sales and lower incident costs), so the operating ratio improved 10.1 points to 66.4% and operating income rose 43% and net income 44%. Management notes the improvement came "primarily as a result of lower railway operating expenses," with 5% higher volumes.
- **Two-year view:** efficiency and profitability remain below 2022 levels — the operating ratio is still 4.1 points worse than 2022 and operating margin 4.2 points lower.

**Caveats**
- The 2023 figures are heavily distorted by the one-time incident. On the company's adjusted (non-GAAP) basis, 2023 operating ratio was 67.4% and adjusted operating income $3,967M; adjusted 2024 operating ratio was 65.8% and adjusted operating income $4,146M (+5% YoY). Adjusted 2023 operating income was still 18% below 2022.
- Ratios above are my calculations from disclosed GAAP values (revenue tag RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax; OperatingIncomeLoss; CostsAndExpenses; NetIncomeLoss), not directly reported fields; the operating ratio itself is also disclosed in the filing (66.4% / 76.5% / 62.3%) and matches my computation.
- Sources: financial_facts for CIK 702165, accession 0000702165-25-000008 (FY2024 10-K); report text chunks 702165/nsc-20241231:115200, :120000, :38400, :113600.
